profile.entities: SRM Contractors Ltd (Parent); Maccaferri Infrastructure Pvt Ltd (MIPL - 51% Subsidiary)
profile.subseg: Slope Stabilization; Tunneling & High-Altitude Roads; Landslide Remediation
profile.themes: Border Infrastructure; Slope Stabilization Moat; Order Book Re-rating; Capex-led Growth

deepdive.sec: Specialized EPC / High-Altitude & Slope Stabilization Infrastructure

bull_bear.body: No equity dilution/QIP planned in near term; Debt used specifically for equipment tied to projects, cleared upon project completion; INR 19 Cr pending payment for final MIPL stake installment due June 2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on large road projects if margin discipline slips; High leverage cycle if project delays occur (though management claims project-specific debt); Competition in road sector is intense; International expansion remains unproven (no orders yet).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident; Emphasizes 'cherry-picking' projects to maintain margins; Proud of technical moat in high-altitude/border regions; Transparent about accounting reclassifications; Aggressive on capex to capture pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The reported INR 1,884 Cr order book is outdated; the real unexecuted book is INR 3,000 Cr as of May 2026 due to post-March wins; The drop in Q4 gross margin is purely an accounting artifact (reclassification) not operational deterioration; MIPL post-acquisition PAT margin (9.4-10.8%) is significantly higher than pre-acquisition (6.7%).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Gross Debt-Equity ratio reduced to 0.33 as of 30th June 2026, which management attributes to reduction in debt levels post-listing reflecting commitment to efficient capital allocation.
- CARE Edge Ratings upgraded both Long-Term and Short-Term Bank Facility ratings from A- Stable to A Stable (effective 1st July 2026).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Slope Stabilization: 51% of order book, strike rate 33-50%, margins 'much better' than roads; Roads: Competitive (strike rate 5-7%), but company cherry-picks high-margin hill/border projects (Ladakh/J&K) avoiding low-margin plains work; Tunnels: Niche high-altitude expertise (Galwan, Hanle).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for specialized high-altitude and slope stabilization expertise in border regions which generalist EPCs cannot execute efficiently. | SRM Contractors Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of own order book surge to INR 3,000 Cr and 51% mix from high-margin slope projects; unique moat in Ladakh/J&K terrain. |
| Rising demand for geo-engineering and gabion solutions for landslide prone areas across India. | Maccaferri Infrastructure Pvt Ltd (MIPL) | beneficiary | High | 51% owned subsidiary contributing INR 850 Cr to order book; post-acquisition margins improved to ~10%; synergies in material sourcing. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- 18+ years of expertise in roadways, tunnels, bridges and slope stabilization across India's toughest terrains, with 53+ projects executed and recognized regional leadership in the J&K & Ladakh region.
- Operates in a high-margin, high-entry-barrier hilly terrain EPC niche, trusted by NHAI, NHIDCL, BRO and State Governments.
- Holds record-breaking engineering credentials: India's tallest railway loading wall (Reasi, J&K), India's longest precast cut-and-cover tunnel (Leh, 12,300 ft) and India's highest underground cavern (Hanle, 15,200 ft, for Indian Army/BRO).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired a 51% stake in Maccaferri Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. (MIPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of an Italian multinational operating in 100+ countries, to strengthen geotechnical/environmental capabilities (slope stabilization, soil retention, erosion control), broaden PAN-India and overseas reach, and add to consolidated order book and financial strength.
- [Recognition] MD Puneet Pal Singh received the 'ET Young Industry Leaders 2025' award; the company won the ET Infra Leadership Award 2025 for 'Excellence in Border/Remote/Hilly Region Infrastructure' and the 'Rashtriya Ratna Samman 2026' for EPC Contractor of the Year.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA margin 8.1% is anomalous due to auditor-mandated reclassification of direct wages into COGS; Management guides 16-18% EBITDA and ~11% PAT for FY27; Slope projects command superior margins vs roads; MoRTH price escalation clauses cover 80-85% of bitumen/diesel cost volatility.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY27 Revenue: INR 1,500-1,750 Cr (+45-55%); EBITDA Margin: 16-18%; PAT Margin: ~11%; Order Inflow Target: INR 2,000 Cr; Capex: INR 250 Cr planned for machinery.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Current unexecuted book at INR 3,000 Cr (INR 2,112 Cr SRM + INR 850 Cr MIPL); Mix: 51% Slope Stabilization (high margin), ~40% Roads/Bridges, 2% Tunnels; Recent wins include INR 483 Cr Nashik Ring Road and INR 128 Cr NHAI landslide project; Pipeline: INR 6,000 Cr with 60-70% conversion expected in FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Geographic expansion into GCC/Africa via Abu Dhabi office (negotiations ongoing in Oman/UAE, no revenue projected yet); Deepening presence in Northeast India for slope works; Potential HAM project entry (currently 0% exposure).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SRM Contractors delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with 96% YoY revenue growth and 120% PAT jump, driven by high-margin slope stabilization projects and the consolidation of MIPL. The key inflection is the order book re-rating to INR 3,000 Cr (up from reported INR 1,884 Cr) with a 51% share from high-margin slope works, supporting a guided 45-55% revenue CAGR and margin expansion to 16-18% EBITDA in FY27.
